title: Valid anagram
summary: Return true if `second` uses exactly the same characters as `first`, each the same number of times.
hints: If the two strings have different lengths, what do you already know? If the lengths match, what must be true about each letter?
Two strings are anagrams exactly when every character appears the same number of times in both.
Count the characters of the first string up, count the second string down, and check that every count ends at zero. Sorting both strings and comparing them also works.
takeaway: Counting is O(n); sorting both strings is O(n log n) and shorter to write. Either passes. In an interview, say the trade-off out loud.
